title: Climate Cooperation and Spatial Industrial Relocation: Stability, Emissions, and Regional Policy Incentives
summary: Climate policy changes production costs and can reshape the geography of production. We study this spatial channel in a focused model where mobile industrial activity responds to local attractiveness, agglomeration strengthens attractiveness, and carbon policy lowers the profitability of emissions-intensive locations. The model yields an explicit carbon-policy threshold separating spatial instability from stability.
